system.name: DAIG (Domain-Adaptive In-context Generation)
system.one_liner: Adapts a pretrained text-to-image model's in-context ability to a target domain with few-shot samples and CIR-LoRA, so it generates unbiased composed-image-retrieval triplets for training.

content.variant_note: prior zero-shot in-context generation (a) stacked above the proposed domain-adaptive version (b), each closed by a tick/cross verdict row; two titled sample galleries on the right
content.argues: Zero-shot in-context generation gives well-aligned but domain-unadapted, biased triplets; adding CIR-LoRA from few-shot samples makes the generator domain- and task-adapted, unbiased and efficient, as the galleries show.
content.subject: Two lettered pipelines around one text-to-image model (frozen use vs LoRA fine-tuning) beside galleries of generated fashion and real-life image-pair triplets.

lessons.what_to_learn: Contrast prior and proposed pipelines as two lettered lanes that reuse one model glyph, change only the adapter, and end each lane in a tick/cross verdict row. Then let titled galleries of real outputs, each with a coloured edit-type caption, carry the quality claim.
lessons.suits: Motivation figures for data-synthesis or fine-tuning methods that fix a failure of a prior generator, where outputs are images paired with short texts.

evidence: textual triplets are first generated by an LLM and inserted into a layout template
DAIG fine-tunes the T2I model with few-shot samples via a novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique, CIR- LoRA.
Representative triplets generated by DAIG are shown on the right side of Figure 1.

summary: DAIG (Domain-Adaptive In-context Generation) adapts the in-context ability of a pretrained text-to-image model to a target domain with few-shot samples, then turns LLM-written textual triplets into synthetic composed-image-retrieval triplets for training. Figure 1 is a motivation figure. On the left, panel (a) shows zero-shot in-context generation: an LLM-made triplet fills a layout template, a T2I model draws a left-right image that is cropped, and a verdict row marks it well aligned but not domain-adapted and biased. Panel (b) reuses the same model glyph with a CIR-LoRA adapter (flame icon) trained on few-shot samples (a Borzoi photo pair) with a flow-matching objective, ending in a green tick for adapted, unbiased and efficient. On the right, two dotted galleries of fashion and real-life image pairs, each with a typed edit caption, show the triplets DAIG generates.
summary_zh: DAIG 用少量样本把文生图模型的上下文生成能力适配到目标领域，合成组合图像检索的三元组。图 1 左侧 (a) 为零样本生成流程并标出偏差，(b) 加入 CIR-LoRA 并以勾选标出优点；右侧是时尚与真实场景两组生成的图像对及编辑说明。
notes: The prior pass listed contribution-mosaic as a third kind; dropped because the right-hand cards are example outputs of the method, not separate contributions (kept as scope-overview example gallery). The first LLM logo looks like Qwen's mark (uncertain). The roles of the Upscale box, the orange versus purple model colours and the end bars are not explained in the figure or the quoted text. The two domain icons are probably vector (stock office-style icons); not checked for the shirt.
